html:
The Lama Lama are an Aboriginal Australian people of Princess Charlotte Bay on the eastern side of the Cape York Peninsula. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country runs from the coast and mangroves inland across wetlands and grassy plains. Much of it is now in a national park that the Lama Lama help to manage. The Palmer River gold rush of the 1870s and the cattle stations that followed pushed many of them off their land in the late 1800s and 1900s. Neighbours on the map include the Mutumui, the Bakanh and the Kaantju. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
